title: Inference economics & budget sprint - SummitBridge intake
summary: Discovery focused on per-token unit economics, choices between hosted/dedicated/private, and how batching, KV caching and quantization move the cost needle. Customer has strict compliance requirements (SOC2 + KMS) and a hard monthly inference budget; next steps are pricing spreadsheet, security evidence, and a perf pilot for 100 QPS mixed-chat workload.
action_items: Maya Chen: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and sample cost model (tokens/day scenarios) by 2027-01-03
Diego Alvarez: Provide benchmark config + required sample payloads and propose perf test window for 100 QPS pilot by 2027-01-04
Priya Shah (customer): Share list of required compliance artifacts and KMS/HSM constraints by 2027-01-05
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing spreadsheet and security pack
Schedule 60m engineering pilot planning call (Redwood SE + SummitBridge infra) week of Jan 4
Run 2-day perf pilot for 100 QPS mixed chat and send results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-29 15:00 PST — 54 minutes. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood here, i have Diego with me, our solutions engineer. How's everyone on the call?
[00:06] Lara Kim: Hi Maya, Lara here. Thanks for making time.
[00:08] Omar Nadeem: Omar. We have about an hour, lots to cover on costing.
[00:11] Priya Shah: Priya — i'll be listening for the compliance bits.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: unit economics — per token price and how batching and KV caching change the math; hosting options (hosted, dedicated, private) and tradeoffs; compliance fit and pilot next steps. Sound good?
[00:23] Lara Kim: Yup. Our main constraint is a hard monthly inference budget — we want to estimate cost for our assistant product at 1M messages/month to start, then scale. We also have to decide if we go hosted first or dedicated.
[00:34] Diego Alvarez: Perfect — maybe i can sketch numbers but want to be clear: per-token is the baseline we bill for hosted, but there are levers: batching, prefix / KV cache, and quantization lower per-token GPU time. Those are multiplicative effects on the effective cost.
[00:48] Omar Nadeem: Two quick asks: latency SLOs need to stay under 400ms P95 for the synchronous flows, and we plan to route high-value traffic to lower-latency paths. Also data residency — some logs can't leave our VPC, which pushes us to private for certain flows.
[01:05] Maya Chen: Noted on residency. We support private deployments and VPC peering for Dedicated as well, and you can pin which model runs where. For cost modeling, do you have an average tokens per message estimate?
[01:16] Lara Kim: Roughly 120 tokens in, 350 tokens out on average. But depends on the use-case — agent responses can spike.
[01:25] Diego Alvarez: Ok let's ballpark. If hosted per-token baseline is $0.00009 per token for generation (this is an example — we will send formal pricing), multiply by batching gains. With continuous batching we can amortize kernel overhead; effective per-token goes down if you accept 50–150ms extra latency for some requests.
[01:44] Lara Kim: So batching is basically trading off latency vs token cost?
[01:47] Diego Alvarez: Exactly. You can think of it as the amortized fixed cost per request being split across many tokens. For chat-typo workloads with many short requests, batching helps a lot. For long responses, the impact is smaller.
[01:58] Priya Shah: How about KV cache — we've got a lot of repeated context for certain customers.
[02:02] Diego Alvarez: KV cache avoids recomputation of earlier layers — for multi-turn dialogs where you repeat a prefix, you can drop token cost significantly because you only compute the new tokens. In practice we've seen 30–70% token-equivalent savings depending on retention windows.
[02:17] Lara Kim: That 70% seems high, can you show an example?
[02:19] Diego Alvarez: Sure: imagine a 1k-token conversation with 50 tokens new per turn. If you cache the key/value states, you only execute the 50 new tokens, so the per-message GPU time is near the new token count plus small overhead. For a 1M message/month baseline that compounds.
[02:34] Omar Nadeem: And quantization? Are you recommending int8 or similar? Does that affect model accuracy?
[02:39] Diego Alvarez: We recommend mixed precision quantization steps. For some models, int8/4-bit quantization reduces memory and bandwidth, which reduces batch sizes you can pack on a GPU and hence costs. There is an accuracy knob and we include eval sets to quantify regression. Many customers accept minimal delta for a 20–40% cost reduction.
[02:56] Lara Kim: So we need to weigh accuracy vs cost — likely ok to accept small deltas for lower tier traffic.
[03:01] Maya Chen: Totally. Many clients adopt tiering: high-fidelity model on dedicated or private for premium users; lower-cost quantized variants for bulk traffic on hosted or dedicated spot pools.
[03:12] Lara Kim: Can you explain dedicated pricing vs hosted? We have aggressive month commit constraints.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Hosted is usage-based: you pay per token/embedding and get zero infra management. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model: you buy a pool of GPUs or throughput with a monthly reservation; effective per-token is lower if you run at steady state but you need the commit. We can show commit tiers and break-even points — e.g., if you sustain X tokens/day, dedicated pays off after Y months. We'll include a breakeven worksheet.
[03:40] Omar Nadeem: Do dedicated pools support VPC and KMS integration?
[03:44] Maya Chen: Yes — Dedicated supports VPC peering and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; Private deployment gives you even more control (on-prem or customer-managed infra) if the residency and control are strict.
[03:54] Priya Shah: For compliance: we need SOC2 type II evidence, encryption at rest, audit logs, and the KMS workflow. How do you deliver that for hosted?
[04:03] Maya Chen: For hosted we provide SOC2 docs, whitepapers, and audit excerpts. For Dedicated you get additional audit logs and network isolation. For Private we hand you the package to deploy in your environment and we provide the control-plane interactions. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[04:16] Lara Kim: Good. Let's talk numbers — if we model 1M messages/month with 470 tokens per message (in+out), that's 470M tokens/month. What's the hosted bill ballpark?
[04:30] Diego Alvarez: Using a hypothetical $0.00009 per token that's ~ $42,300/month before caching and batching effects. With caching and batching we commonly see 20–60% effective reduction depending on patterns — so say $17k–34k range. But we will model your actual distributions and show ranges.
[04:52] Lara Kim: We have a cap of $20k/mo initial — so we need to demonstrate hitting under that or propose a hybrid routing.
[04:59] Maya Chen: Hybrid routing is common: route high-value customers to Dedicated/private pools, everything else to hosted cheaper tiers, enable KV cache aggressively for the bulk, and apply quantization for lower tier models. This is how you maintain SLOs while hitting cost ceilings.
[05:13] Omar Nadeem: If we do dedicated, what's the typical commit size? We can't commit to 100% utilization, we need burst capacity too.
[05:20] Maya Chen: Typical commitments start at equivalent of a 4–8 GPU pool for small enterprise pilots; we also offer burst credits for spike handling. The exact commit depends on model family and latency SLO. We'll propose a pilot commit scenario with burstable add-ons.
[05:33] Diego Alvarez: For the perf pilot we recommend a 48–72 hour window with synthetic traffic matching your token distribution and some real sample payloads. That gives us a real-world tokens/sec curve and cost per token under multiple configs.
[05:44] Priya Shah: You mentioned audit logs — can we retain logs in our S3 for 7 years?
[05:49] Maya Chen: Yes for Dedicated and Private we can ship audit logs to your S3. For hosted we have retention tiers and can push to customer buckets for longer retention. We'll include retention styling and cost in the security pack.
[05:59] Lara Kim: Ok, what about fallback policies? If a dedicated pool is overloaded do requests fail or route to hosted?
[06:06] Diego Alvarez: We have smart routing and fallback: you can set policies to route to hosted model variants, to a degraded quantized model, or to queue with a timeout. Many customers configure graceful fallback to keep user experience consistent.
[06:18] Omar Nadeem: We'll need deterministic latency for premium flows; fallback should be disabled for those.
[06:22] Maya Chen: That’s straightforward to configure per-route.
[06:25] Lara Kim: Let's talk concrete next steps — what will you send after this call?
[06:29] Maya Chen: We'll send a package: 1) Hosted vs Dedicated pricing sheet with example scenarios; 2) Security pack (SOC2, KMS integration guide, audit log options); 3) Proposed perf pilot plan and bench config. Diego will send the benchmark payload generator and the test harness.
[06:42] Priya Shah: We need to see cryptographic attestation for KMS/HSM — we use an HSM provider and require specific key policies.
[06:49] Diego Alvarez: We'll include a KMS integration checklist and reach out to your security team directly if needed.
[06:54] Lara Kim: On timing — we want to kick a pilot in January. Is week of Jan 4 realistic?
[06:59] Maya Chen: Yes that works— we'll aim to have the pricing + security pack out by Jan 3 so infra can review before the pilot.
[07:06] Omar Nadeem: One more question — do you provide per-route token-level cost attribution? We want to slice budget by product feature.
[07:11] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console offers token-level cost breakdowns per route/model and you can export to CSV or integrate with billing. We can show a demo in the pilot planning call.
[07:21] Lara Kim: Can you also show the break-even calculation for dedicated commit vs hosted? We need that for our finance team.
[07:27] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we'll include breakeven cases at different utilization levels and retention.
[07:31] Diego Alvarez: Quick note: the math usually simplifies to comparing your expected sustained tokens/day times hosted price vs reserved monthly capacity amortized plus predicted utilization inefficiency. We'll surface assumptions so finance can tweak them.
[07:45] Priya Shah: If we go private for regulated flows, what is turnaround time for on-prem package?
[07:50] Maya Chen: Private deployments vary — small pilots can be done in 4–8 weeks, larger regulated rollouts longer. We'll put an estimate in the security pack.
[07:59] Lara Kim: Ok good.
[08:00] [Longer sections of technical back-and-forth omitted for brevity in summary — includes Diego walking through sample cost model, token math spreadsheet, and an example KV cache retention policy] 
[28:34] Diego Alvarez: ...So on slide three of the example spreadsheet you can see the sensitivity to median response length — median length up to 600 tokens doubles hosted costs if no caching used.
[28:42] Lara Kim: That matches our internal sims — interesting.
[28:45] Omar Nadeem: For the pilot payloads, do you need PII redacted?
[28:49] Diego Alvarez: Yes please redact PII — our bench can accept synthetic tokens or redacted traces.
[28:53] Priya Shah: We'll produce a sample with redacted customer IDs and hashed user IDs.
[29:00] Lara Kim: Can you also show us a recommended routing policy example? We want to see rule examples like "premium_user -> private pool; regular_user -> hosted" with thresholds.
[29:08] Maya Chen: We'll include sample routing policy YAML and a diagram.
[29:12] Lara Kim: What's the invoicing model for dedicated? Monthly or annual?
[29:16] Maya Chen: Monthly is common for pilots; we offer discounts for annual commitments.
[29:20] Omar Nadeem: Anything else on the cost side we should be aware of? Hidden costs?
[29:25] Diego Alvarez: Watch data egress/cold start of KV cache if using private infra across regions. Also, retention of logs and long-term storage adds to totals. We'll include these line items in the cost model.
[29:36] Lara Kim: Great. I'm taking notes.
[29:39] Priya Shah: A compliance question — do you allow Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)?
[29:44] Maya Chen: Yes — Dedicated and Private can support BYOK/HSM. For hosted we provide KMS integration patterns and sometimes BYOK depending on region and provider. We'll detail options in the security pack.
[29:56] Omar Nadeem: For the perf pilot, what metrics will you collect?
[30:00] Diego Alvarez: Latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, effective cost per token, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, and model regression checks against your eval set.
[30:10] Lara Kim: And the output — will you provide a CSV with per-request cost mapping?
[30:13] Diego Alvarez: Yes we'll export per-request attributes and aggregate cost buckets.
[30:17] Maya Chen: Ok, final recap: Redwood will send pricing worksheet and security artifacts by Jan 3; schedule the pilot planning call week of Jan 4; pilot run (48–72 hrs) thereafter; customer to supply redacted sample payloads and compliance checklist. Any other items?
[30:33] Lara Kim: That covers it.
[30:35] Priya Shah: Sounds good. We'll review the pack and get back.
[30:38] Omar Nadeem: Thanks, looking forward.
[30:40] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
[30:45] [call ends — 54m total per header]
